About

I am an applied economist working at the intersection of agriculture, environment, health, and development. My research focuses on productivity, climate and sustainability policies, and One Health, with the aim of providing practical, policy-relevant evidence for low- and middle-income countries.

I am particularly interested in how agrifood systems can improve livelihoods and economic growth while addressing public health risks and environmental constraints.

I hold a PhD in Economics from the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) and a BSc in Economics from Jimma University, and I have been a visiting scholar at the University of Western Australia. My academic and professional experience spans Europe, Africa, Asia, and Latin America, combining rigorous quantitative methods with a strong policy orientation.

Currently, I work as an economist at the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), where I contribute to global and country-level analysis on antimicrobial resistance economics, livestock productivity, climate mitigation and adaptation, and agrifood investment strategies. My work links micro-level evidence with economy-wide modelling to understand trade-offs, identify priority investments, and provide practical inputs for policymaking in low- and middle-income countries, especially in settings facing structural constraints and high uncertainty.

My research is published in journals including Nature Communications, Agricultural Economics, Energy Economics, and Energy Policy.

Publications

Professional Engagements

High-Level Policy and Investment Dialogue on Dairy Methane Emission Reduction in Mongolia

📍 Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia📅 August 3–7, 2026

Led the technical discussions on leveraging economic evidence to advance dairy methane emission reduction in Mongolia during an FAO high-level policy and investment dialogue under the Knowledge for Investment (K4I) project. Presented and discussed preliminary findings from farm-level assessments, Marginal Abatement Cost (MAC) analysis, and the Livestock Policy Simulation Model (LPSM), engaging government representatives, development partners, researchers, and dairy-sector stakeholders on the costs, benefits, and trade-offs of low-emission dairy technologies. The discussions focused on translating analytical evidence into practical livestock and climate policy options, investment priorities, and support for Mongolia's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The mission also included bilateral consultations and field visits to better align policy recommendations with dairy farmers' production realities.

High-Level Technical Workshop on Antimicrobial Use Mitigation and RENOFARM Implementation

📍 Lusaka, Zambia📅 August 16-24, 2025

Served as FAO technical lead for a high-level mission in Zambia supporting efforts to advance antimicrobial use (AMU) mitigation in livestock. The mission contextualized FAO's microeconomic optimization framework within Farmer Field School (FFS) programmes and supported its application under the RENOFARM initiative (Reducing the Need for Antimicrobials in Agrifood Systems), aligned with national AMR priorities. Senior-level policy dialogue and technical discussions with line ministries (Livestock, Health), national public health authorities, academia, development partners, producer organizations, and the private sector contributed to consensus on FFS as a key delivery mechanism for AMU reduction, and on next-step analytical work to assess behavioral change, productivity impacts, and investment implications.

Training and Capacity Building on Productivity and Efficiency Analysis in Livestock Production

📍 Hanoi, Vietnam📅 July 3-7, 2023

Delivered hands-on capacity-building training for the General Statistics Office of Vietnam (GSO) and the Institute of Policy and Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development (IPSARD) on productivity and efficiency analysis in the livestock sector, with a strong focus on Stochastic Frontier Models (SFM/SFA) using STATA.
